text:
jules: Heads-up  new CloudEdge ad popped up claiming 'universal inference, no tuning' with a flashy latency chart. We need a concise internal rebut + SDR soundbites for tomorrow's webinar.
mona: thanks. can someone grab screenshots?
diego: got 'em. link in thread. main claims: 'works on any infra', 'zero tuning', 'faster than typical GPUs'.
sara: core approach: emphasize serving-first reality. 'any infra' ignores cache, batching, and kernel choices.
anil: SDR-ready quick bullets: [tech buyer] 'Runtime tuned to model shape and traffic patterns; measurable p50 improvements.' [biz buyer] 'Consistent latency & transparent cost controls across deployments.'
jules: can we keep SDR lines to one short sentence each?
diego: proposed micro-rebut for SDR chat: 
```
CloudEdge: 'no tuning'
Redwood: 'We tune kernels and caching to your model & workload so real apps see lower latency and cost.'
```
sara: shorter: 'Redwood tunes runtime for your workload  not one-size-fits-all.' (typo fix)
anil: webinar slide bullets (3):
- Predictable latency via reserved capacity & routing policies
- Lower unit-costs through batching, caching, and quantization guidance
- Full observability: token-level cost and latency breakdowns
mona: observability line is gold. any metric examples? keep vague to avoid legal.
diego: say 'measurable latency wins and meaningful cost reductions in production' 
jules: action items:
- @anil: draft 2x SDR 1-liners (tech + biz) due 2pm PT
- @sara: one slide for webinar with 3 bullets + short note about 'any infra' oversimplification due EOD
- @diego: drop quick battle snippets into Notion + tag SDR leads due EOD
ops-bot: Reminder set: Drafts due 14:00 PT today (channel: #marketing).
mona: thanks all  keep it crisp and un-jargony. :thumbsup:
